label: Organograms: posts, grades and pay
one_row_is: one post (senior) or one group of posts at a grade under a senior post (junior) in a public body's organogram, as last published

columns.name: body
columns.meaning: the public body whose organogram this is, as the index names the publisher

columns.name: level
columns.meaning: 'senior' (one row is one post, Senior Civil Service or equivalent) or 'junior' (one row is a number of posts at one grade reporting to one senior post)

columns.name: as_of
columns.meaning: the date the organogram is a snapshot of, read from the file's name (central government reports at 31 March and 30 September)

columns.name: post_reference
columns.meaning: the body's own reference for a senior post (Post Unique Reference); junior rows have none

columns.name: job_title
columns.meaning: the post's title as published (a senior post's Job Title; a junior group's Generic Job Title); 'REDACTED' or 'N/D' is kept as published

columns.name: grade
columns.meaning: the grade or equivalent as published (SCS1-4, G6, G7, SEO, HEO, EO, AO, AA, or the body's own scale)

columns.name: unit
columns.meaning: the unit, directorate or team the post sits in, as published

columns.name: organisation
columns.meaning: the organisation named in the file (an agency or arm's-length body may report under a parent department)

columns.name: parent_department
columns.meaning: the parent department named in the file

columns.name: reports_to
columns.meaning: the post_reference of the senior post this post or group reports to; 'XX' marks the head of the body

columns.name: pay_floor_gbp
columns.meaning: the bottom of the pay band as published: a senior post's Actual Pay Floor (£5,000 bands), a junior grade's Payscale Minimum

columns.name: pay_ceiling_gbp
columns.meaning: the top of the pay band as published: Actual Pay Ceiling, or Payscale Maximum

columns.name: pay_band
columns.meaning: a pay band published as text where a body gives one ('£180,000 to £184,999') instead of a floor and ceiling

columns.name: fte
columns.meaning: full-time equivalent: the senior post's FTE, or the junior group's Number of Posts in FTE

columns.name: salary_cost_of_reports_gbp
columns.meaning: a senior post's Salary Cost of Reports as published: the total pay of the staff under it

columns.name: job_function
columns.meaning: the senior post's Job/Team Function as published

columns.name: notes
columns.meaning: the file's notes column, as published

rules: The table is posts, not people. The senior file names the holder of each post by statute; that column is not taken, nor are contact phone numbers or e-mail addresses. Whether names join the table is a separate decision (FAMILIES.md), not a consequence of the licence.

Central government files follow the Cabinet Office organogram standard: a senior file (one row per post) and a junior file (one row per grade under a senior post, with a number of posts). Both are mapped to this one shape; 'level' says which a row came from.
The newest senior and the newest junior file of a body are the family's source, taken by the date in the file's name; older snapshots stay findable in the index.
Pay is kept as published: senior pay in the £5,000 band the body reported, junior pay as the grade's scale. 'N/A' and 'N/D' become an empty cell, never zero.

Councils' senior-salary tables under the transparency code are mapped only where a person has matched their columns to this shape; a table that lists people rather than posts is mapped without the name columns.
